Title: Last Ferry Receipt
Author: CineForge evaluation source author
Credit: Synthetic evaluation fixture

INT. FERRY TICKET OFFICE - NIGHT

The last sailing has been cancelled. A shuttered ticket window faces empty benches. LENA, the clerk, numbers a paper envelope 17 and slides a brass locker key inside. Her left thumb wears a fresh white bandage. TOM, her younger brother, sets a blue insulated medicine case on the counter.

TOM
Dad's doses. The clinic launch comes at six. Don't leave this in the locker.

Lena puts the envelope in her coat and the case beneath the counter. Through frosted glass, a COURIER in an orange rain cape knocks twice. Only a silhouette is visible.

COURIER (O.S.)
Seventeen. North locker. Before the tide turns.

LENA
Who sent you?

The silhouette retreats without answering. Tom reaches for the case, but Lena stops him.

LENA
I'll take it to the launch myself. You lock up here.

She lifts the blue case and goes. Tom stays behind with the shutter crank.

EXT. FERRY PIER - LATER

Fog erases the far bank. Lena sets the blue medicine case on a mooring bollard. She removes envelope 17, takes out the brass key, and unlocks a green locker marked NORTH. Inside lies a small metal cash box. She leaves the empty envelope inside the locker, pockets the key, and carries the cash box to the bollard.

An OLD MAN in an orange rain cape stands by the gangway. His face is visible; the earlier courier's was not.

OLD MAN
You found it, then.

LENA
Were you at my window?

OLD MAN
Windows aren't much use in this fog.

He turns away. A ferry horn sounds from the river, although no vessel can be seen. Lena opens the cash box. It contains a photograph of two children beside a ferry and a folded receipt. On the receipt: STORAGE PAID THROUGH FRIDAY. She puts both back, shuts the box, and takes it and the blue case toward the boathouse.

INT. RESCUE BOATHOUSE - PRE-DAWN

RUTH, the launch pilot, checks a wall clock: 5:50. Lena arrives carrying both containers. Ruth notices the white bandage, now grey with grime, before taking the medicine case.

RUTH
Your father still at the clinic?

LENA
Until the launch brings him home.

Ruth places the blue case in a refrigerator. Lena keeps the cash box under her arm. Tom calls from a wall telephone; his voice comes through its speaker.

TOM (PHONE)
The office is locked. Someone left an orange cape on the bench outside.

LENA
Leave it there. We don't know whose it is.

Lena asks Ruth to keep the case cold until departure. Ruth agrees. The clock ticks toward six. No passenger arrives.

EXT. FERRY PIER - DAWN

Lena returns with the cash box, without the medicine case. The refrigerator remains behind in the boathouse. Her soiled bandage has not changed. The green locker stands open; empty envelope 17 lies inside.

She puts the cash box back in the locker and locks it with the brass key. Tom joins her empty-handed from the ticket office path. Lena gives him the key.

TOM
Was that Dad in the photograph?

LENA
Could be. It didn't have a date or names.

They watch Ruth steer the clinic launch away from the boathouse. Ruth waves. No one else is visible aboard.

He turns away. A ferry horn sounds from the river, although no vessel can be seen. Lena opens the cash box. It contains a photograph of two children beside a ferry and a folded receipt. On the receipt: STORAGE PAID THROUGH FRIDAY. She puts both back, shuts the box, and takes it and the blue case toward the boathouse.

INT. RESCUE BOATHOUSE - PRE-DAWN

RUTH, the launch pilot, checks a wall clock: 5:50. Lena arrives carrying both containers. Ruth notices the white bandage, now grey with grime, before taking the medicine case.

RUTH
Your father still at the clinic?

LENA
Until the launch brings him home.

Ruth places the blue case in a refrigerator. Lena keeps the cash box under her arm. Tom calls from a wall telephone; his voice comes through its speaker.

TOM (PHONE)
The office is locked. Someone left an orange cape on the bench outside.

LENA
Leave it there. We don't know whose it is.

Lena asks Ruth to keep the case cold until departure. Ruth agrees. The clock ticks toward six. No passenger arrives.

EXT. FERRY PIER - DAWN

Lena returns with the cash box, without the medicine case. The refrigerator remains behind in the boathouse. Her soiled bandage has not changed. The green locker stands open; empty envelope 17 lies inside.

She puts the cash box back in the locker and locks it with the brass key. Tom joins her empty-handed from the ticket office path. Lena gives him the key.

TOM
Was that Dad in the photograph?

LENA
Could be. It didn't have a date or names.

They watch Ruth steer the clinic launch away from the boathouse. Ruth waves. No one else is visible aboard.

elements.content: INT. FERRY TICKET OFFICE - NIGHT

The last sailing has been cancelled. A shuttered ticket window faces empty benches. LENA, the clerk, numbers a paper envelope 17 and slides a brass locker key inside. Her left thumb wears a fresh white bandage. TOM, her younger brother, sets a blue insulated medicine case on the counter.
TOM
Dad's doses. The clinic launch comes at six. Don't leave this in the locker.
Lena puts the envelope in her coat and the case beneath the counter. Through frosted glass, a COURIER in an orange rain cape knocks twice. Only a silhouette is visible.
COURIER (O.S.)
Seventeen. North locker. Before the tide turns.
LENA
Who sent you?
The silhouette retreats without answering. Tom reaches for the case, but Lena stops him.
LENA
I'll take it to the launch myself. You lock up here.
She lifts the blue case and goes. Tom stays behind with the shutter crank.

An unseen Courier in an orange rain cape knocks and calls out the exact number 17 and locker location before retreating without answering Lena's question. The silhouette and unanswered identity create immediate suspense and imply a covert network.

Lena stops Tom from reclaiming the medicine case and asserts she will personally deliver it to the launch, separating herself from Tom and taking sole responsibility for both the case and the mystery of the courier.

data.central_conflict: The central conflict is between Lena's duty to protect her father and her inability to understand the true nature of the mysterious exchange she's been drawn into. She must decide whether to trust strangers and follow cryptic instructions while protecting her family's welfare, all while operating with incomplete information about what is actually happening and why.
data.logline: A ferry clerk must navigate a mysterious midnight exchange involving a hidden cash box and cryptic strangers to protect her ailing father and uncover the truth behind an enigmatic photograph.
data.narrative_arc: The story follows a tight, mysterious arc that begins with a simple task—delivering medicine—and spirals into an enigmatic exchange involving hidden keys, mysterious photographs, and cryptic strangers. The narrative builds tension through fog-shrouded settings and incomplete information, creating a sense of unease and uncertainty. Rather than resolving the central mystery, the story ends ambiguously, with the photograph's meaning and the father's true whereabouts remaining unknown. The arc is one of escalating questions rather than answers, leaving the audience in the same state of uncertainty as the protagonist.
data.protagonist_journey: Lena begins as a dutiful ferry clerk performing routine tasks, but is drawn into a mysterious exchange that tests her judgment and loyalty. Throughout the night, she must navigate between protecting her family, following cryptic instructions, and maintaining her own agency. She evolves from a passive worker into an active participant in an unexplained scheme, yet remains fundamentally uncertain about her choices. By dawn, she has completed the exchange but gained no clarity, suggesting a journey toward acceptance of ambiguity rather than resolution.
data.setting_overview: The story takes place over a single night and into dawn at a remote ferry terminal during fog. The primary locations are the shuttered ferry ticket office, the fog-shrouded pier, and a rescue boathouse. The world is one of maritime isolation, where a clinic launch serves as the only connection to medical care. The fog is both literal and metaphorical—obscuring vision, identity, and truth. The time period appears contemporary or slightly ambiguous, grounded in the practical details of ferry operations and medical logistics.
data.synopsis: On the night of the last ferry sailing, Lena, a ticket clerk with a fresh hand injury, receives an unexpected delivery: her brother Tom brings their father's medicine for the clinic launch arriving at dawn. A mysterious courier appears at the shuttered ticket window with instructions to retrieve envelope 17 from the north locker before the tide turns. Lena discovers the envelope contains a brass key that unlocks a cash box holding only a photograph of two children by a ferry and a storage receipt. As she navigates between the ticket office, pier, and boathouse through fog-shrouded night, Lena must decide whether to trust the strangers involved in this exchange and what the photograph's significance means for her family. By dawn, she returns the cash box to the locker, the medicine safely delivered to the launch pilot Ruth, and watches the clinic boat depart with no passengers aboard—leaving the mystery of the photograph and her father's true whereabouts unresolved.
